finding.claim: purge() calls checkPerm(u, "admin") but ignores its boolean return value, so the admin permission is never enforced and purgeAll() runs for any caller that reaches the handler.
finding.source: HTTP request to the purge handler; the caller's identity comes from userFrom(r) (handlers.go:40), which is the request context user. The attacker is any authenticated user whose Perms map lacks "admin".
finding.sink: purgeAll() (handlers.go:27, destructive operation, stub here), reached unconditionally after the discarded check.

trace.note: u := userFrom(r) loads the caller from request context
checkPerm(u, "admin") evaluated; result discarded (Go permits calling a function and ignoring a bool return), so no return/abort
responds "purged" with 200 to the non-admin caller

finding.guards_checked: checkPerm (handlers.go:12-14) returns u.Perms[perm] correctly, so the bug is solely that the result is unused. Compare rotateKeys (handlers.go:31-38), which uses mustPerm and returns on failure, so it is not affected. No route registration or auth middleware is in the repo, so I could not verify whether a middleware gate sits in front of /purge. Even if one does, the handler itself enforces nothing beyond authentication, so a non-admin authenticated user can still purge. If the route is mounted in admin-only middleware, severity drops to defense-in-depth.

verdict.guard_found: None in the handler. checkPerm (handlers.go:12-14) returns a bool, but the call at handlers.go:26 is a bare statement, so the result is discarded and nothing aborts before purgeAll() at line 27. The correct pattern is mustPerm at handlers.go:33, which rejects and returns. No route registration or auth middleware exists in the repo, so a gate in front of /purge cannot be ruled out from this code.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the file: userFrom at handlers.go:25, the discarded checkPerm result at handlers.go:26, the unconditional purgeAll() at handlers.go:27, and the 200 response at handlers.go:28. Any authenticated user reaches the effect, and the only check is the discarded return at handlers.go:26, so the flaw holds at the handler level. If route-level admin middleware exists outside this repo, severity drops to defense-in-depth, as the candidate notes.
